root.name: Philidor Defense: Lopez Countergambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. Bc4 f5

overview: Black counterattacks at once with ...f5, offering a pawn to open the f-file and undermine e4. White can take on f5 and e4 with Ng5 and d4 to win material or take space, while Black aims for lines against the e4 pawn and the weakened f2. White has the better chances with sensible development, and the opening is mostly seen as a surprise weapon.

white_ideas.idea: Take on f5 or play Ng5 with pressure on f7 and keep the extra pawn
Develop with d3 or d4 and exploit Black's weakened kingside

black_ideas.idea: Open the f-file with ...fxe4 and hit e4 and f2
Create tactics down the e8-h5 diagonal and play for ...Nf6 development

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Black's f-pawn gone and White the extra pawn

character.notes: Immediate pawn offer and tactics around e4, f2 and f7; both kings exposed.

gambit.notes: White can take on f5 or e4 and keep the pawn with careful play.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious for Black; White's best replies keep an edge.

structure.notes: Open lines on the f-file and diagonals after the exchanges.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever choose it.

level.notes: Trap-heavy and unsound, so not a good first repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Jaenisch Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: A different move order with a wild tactical melee

character.reason: An early pawn offer and open lines make it tactical for both sides.

soundness.reason: Strong players consider the countergambit unsound.

structure.reason: Open lines for the pieces after the pawns come off.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose it at all.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never beginner.

plans.reason: Black plays for activity, White targets f7.
